A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWAP research. All 33 pages of v2 and 28 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison. Relocated and renamed material can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, search-width and search-depth analyses, and appendix efficiency results.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, rollout and breadth analyses, efficiency measurements, and fine-grained appendix results.

M1.justification: v3 adds DPO preference optimization of the discriminator after supervised training, using GPT-4o-labeled response pairs (Appendix D). This introduces a distinct training objective for a key component. The underlying graph planner, diversity equations, shared models, and contextual reframing are retained; their renaming and relocation are not additional method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, and coding tasks through GSM8K, MATH, FOLIO, ReClor, HumanEval, and MBPP. MATH500 retains the existing mathematical subjects and difficulty levels; its selection and reassignment of other examples to training change the split rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: Self-consistency is added to the GSM8K efficiency comparison, although it already appeared in the main evaluations (v2 Table 5; v3 Table 3). Table 2 removes the PRM-instead-of-CR comparator. The principal external comparator set in Table 1 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation changes from the full 5,000-example MATH test set to MATH500, with the remaining 4,500 examples added to training. Self-consistency and PRM rollouts increase from 8 to 32. Planning generation/breadth limits change from 5/8 to 3/3, with 32 total rollouts; non-MATH step limits fall from 10 to 6. CR training groups change from sizes 2 or 3 to 2, and coding training counts are revised. The new scaling analysis uses 200 test examples per dataset and labels its breadth plots Pass@32 accuracy.

E4.justification: The search-attempt and search-depth studies in v2 Figures 4–5 are replaced by rollout and breadth studies covering both base models in v3 Figure 4. Table 2 adds a state-prediction-refinement ablation and removes the PRM-instead-of-CR ablation. Appendix D adds a qualitative full-fine-tuning versus LoRA comparison. Retained output examples are revised, notably the ReClor reasoning and several entailment graphs.

E5.justification: Both versions report ± values in Table 1 and shaded bands in their scaling plots. Neither specifies seeds, repeated-run counts, or clearly defines these uncertainty summaries. Changed numerical uncertainties and replacement plots do not establish a changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced across benchmark, ablation, scaling, and efficiency comparisons. For example, LLaMA3 SWAP GSM8K accuracy changes from 82.7 ± 0.6 to 92.6 ± 0.2, while MATH accuracy changes from 42.3 on the full test set to 43.2 on MATH500. SWAP's reported GSM8K token usage changes from 3,612 to 12.4k. These accompany changed training and evaluation settings and do not establish same-setting performance gains. The ReClor example also changes its assessments of distractors while retaining answer 0.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix F's explicit asymptotic complexity expressions and detailed BFS/DFS/MCTS comparison are removed; v3 Section 4.5 retains a qualitative complexity comparison. The MDP, entailment-graph definitions, and diversity equations remain substantively equivalent. New retrieval notation and the normalization example mainly explain existing operations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that entailment-graph planning, an accurate world model, diversity-based generation, and contrastive ranking improve reasoning across mathematics, logic, and coding. The rewritten abstract and contributions preserve this scientific scope. Changes from DBM to DM and structural to symbolic verification principally revise terminology and emphasis.

C2.justification: v3 adds concerns about calibration of independently assigned PRM scores and explicitly discusses computational demands, adaptive candidate counts, and lighter discriminators in Limitations. Ablation and fine-grained discussions shift their principal attribution from the discriminator to planning. Existing explanations of world-model overhead and errors introduced by deeper simulated futures are retained.

D1.justification: v3 specifies point assignment and comparison-group sampling, clarifies verification placement, describes DPO preference-data construction and fine-tuning choices, and newly discloses temperature 0.7. Appendix D updates training-data counts and generation-model references. Much of the existing reproducibility information, including the two LoRAs, DPR retrieval of five examples, prompts, and code/data access, remains available.

R1.justification: v3 removes the cognitive System 1/System 2 grounding and several associated references, adds DPO and DeepSeek-V3 citations, and expands comparisons with diverse beam search and GFlowNets in Appendix A. Its central positioning relative to planning methods and process reward models remains. Author and publication updates for retained references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around entailment-graph construction. Related Work moves after the experiments, efficiency moves from Appendix F into the main text, and state-diversity and contextual-reframing explanations move into Appendix A. Terminology is revised throughout, and Limitations, Ethics Statement, and Acknowledgments sections are added.

P2.justification: The main text and prose appendices change from single-column to two-column presentation. Figures 1–3 are redrawn, the two earlier scaling figures are replaced by an eight-panel figure, and the separate framework diagram in v2 Figure 6 is removed. Tables and captions are reformatted and relocated, including the efficiency table's move into the main text.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessability through more explicit ranking and training descriptions, clearer diagrams, and a ReClor example that now explains why distractors are unsuitable. The state-refinement ablation and explicit computational limitations also strengthen the presentation. These gains are limited by removal of the direct CR-versus-PRM ablation and search-depth study. Higher reported scores do not independently establish improvement because training, inference budgets, and the MATH split changed.
